descriptionChirho: An open courtyard or court of a building, especially the courtyard of the high priest's palace or of the temple. S63615 (courtyard, 9x) and S63617 (court, 1x) represent the same architectural space. Spanish uses 'patio' and 'atrio' (both = courtyard/court area); Arabic 'دَارِ' and 'دارَ' (dār = house/courtyard) identically; Korean '뜨락' (tteurak = courtyard) in both; Swahili 'ua' (courtyard/compound) uniformly; Hindi 'आँगन/आंगन' (āṅgan = courtyard) throughout. The single S63617 occurrence is simply a low-frequency variant in the same spatial domain.

An enclosed area for keeping sheep — a fold or pen, as in John 10:1,16 where Jesus speaks of the sheep and the fold. This is a distinct sense from the architectural courtyard, confirmed across multiple languages: Spanish 'redil' (sheepfold) vs 'patio' (courtyard); Arabic 'حَظيرَة' (ḥaẓīra = enclosure/pen) vs 'دَارِ' (courtyard); Korean '우리' (uri = animal pen/cage) vs '뜨락' (courtyard); Swahili 'zizi' (animal enclosure/kraal) vs 'ua' (courtyard); Hindi 'बाड़ा/बाड़े' (bāṛā = pen/enclosure) vs 'आँगन' (courtyard). Every language distinguishes these two senses clearly.
